analysis: Examined all five changed files. StartupPreloader.swift (lines 136-139, 157-162, 203-206) only adds two Summary fields (failedInsufficientMemory, notAttempted) and records them. Admission logic, the no-evict rule, fail-open/fail-closed self-test handling and cancellation are unchanged. Log and telemetry contents are unchanged, and the insufficient-memory classifier is untouched. StatusCommand+Residency.swift (lines 45-76) adds two local CLI status formatters, pendingSelectionLines and recoveryLines. They read enabled_models_at_start, enabled_models_at_last_switch and selected_model_recovery from the owner-local daemon state file and print model IDs, timing and a blocker string to the operator's terminal. StatusCommand.swift (lines 150, 173-175) wires these into output. The tests add two CLI fixtures. No changes touch the coordinator WebSocket, attestation, App Attest authorization, key custody, prompt or completion handling, encryption, the prefix cache (T-041) or fan control. Residual notes: the state file is trusted local operator data (TB-003). The blocker string comes from the daemon and is printed unsanitized, which at worst gives terminal-escape or confusion risk against the operator's own state file, not a new boundary crossing. The model IDs shown are already public through heartbeats. Out of scope here are the producers of the new DaemonState fields (selectedModelRecovery, enabledModelsAtStart, enabledModelsAtLastSwitch) and the Dependencies wiring in ProviderLoop+StartupPreload. Neither is in the supplied evidence, so I could not check what the daemon writes into blocker (for example, whether it can contain request content). The visible test fixture shows only model IDs and memory figures. No security regression identified.
